703907.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *deh₃- Proto-Indo-European *-r̥ Proto-Indo-European *dóh₃r̥ Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *déh₃rom Proto-Hellenic *dṓron Ancient Greek δῶρον Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *dṓron, from Proto-Indo-European…

703933.t: Borrowed from Hebrew עִבְרִי (ʿiḇrī, “Hebrew”), likely through Aramaic עִבְרַי (ʿiḇray, “Hebrew”).

703901.t: A regularly declined accusative form of δωρεά (dōreā́, “a gift”, “bounty”), also used as an adverb.

703918.t: Possibly from Proto-Hellenic *ewajō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wéh₂-ye-ti, from the root *h₁weh₂- (“to leave, abandon”). However, the augment of the Classical Greek preterite points to Proto-Hellenic *hewajō.

703922.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hebdmākontə, from Proto-Indo-European *septm̥-ḱómt-h₂, from *septḿ̥(d)ḱomt. Cognates include Sanskrit सप्तति (saptati), Latin septuāgintā and Old Armenian եօթանասուն (eōtʻanasun).

703914.t: From Proto-Hellenic *éhər, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ésh₂r̥. Cognates include Hittite 𒂊𒌍𒄯 (ēšḫar), Sanskrit असृ॑ज् (ásṛj), Old Armenian արիւն (ariwn), Latin sanguis and Old Latin assyr.

703949.t: From Proto-Hellenic *egéřřō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ger- (“to awake”). Cognate with Sanskrit जागृ (jāgṛ, “to be awake, alert”); see the Sanskrit for more cognates.

703925.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hébdomos, from Proto-Indo-European *septm̥mós (“seventh”), with medial voicing (the -bd- cluster) perhaps by influence from the following nasal.

703912.t: Quantitative metathesis of εἰάν (eiắn), itself a univerbation of εἰ (ei) + ἄν (ắn, modal particle).

703948.t: Probably from ἐν (en, “in; at”) + Proto-Indo-European *gew- (“hand; to curve”, whence γυῖον (guîon, “hand”)), ἐγγύη (engŭ́ē, “pledge; security”)), thus literally, “at hand”.

703917.t: Contraction of ἕο αὐτοῦ (héo autoû), literally “his self”.

703900.t: Related to δῶρον (dôron, “gift”), albeit with a suffix -εά (-eā́) of seemingly unclear form and function.

703903.t: From δωρέω (dōréō, “to make a present”) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

703991.t: Unknown. Not related to ἐγκεράννυμι (enkeránnumi, “to mix”).

703945.t: Uncertain. Beekes hesitantly suggest a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *g⁽ʷ⁾ow- (“hand”).

703972.t: From ἐν- (en-) + κεῖμαι (keîmai). Serves as the passive of ἐντίθημι (entíthēmi).

703955.t: From ἐγ- (eg-) + καινός (kainós) + -ια (-ia). Semantic loan from Biblical Hebrew חֲנֻכָּה (ḥănukkâ).

703947.t: From the same stem as ἐγγύη (engúē, “pledge, surety, security”), which see.
